name: ck_pr_rtm_begin
prose: Precondition: the CPU executes RTM (the instruction bytes 0xc7 0xf8 are XBEGIN); the caller must not assume more than the contract below. The function takes no arguments, no locks and allocates no memory. Postcondition (gcc/x86_64/ck_pr_rtm.h:64-76): it initialises r to CK_PR_RTM_STARTED (~0U, line 55) and runs an inline asm that emits XBEGIN with a zero relative offset and takes r as in/out in eax. If the hardware starts a transaction, execution continues after the instruction with eax unchanged, so the function returns ~0U and the caller is then inside the transactional region and must end it with ck_pr_rtm_end or abort it with ck_pr_rtm_abort. If the transaction aborts, the hardware resumes at the fall-through address with eax set by the hardware to the abort status, and the function returns that status; by the RTM definition (not enforced by this C code) bits 0-5 are the CK_PR_RTM_EXPLICIT, _RETRY, _CONFLICT, _CAPACITY, _DEBUG and _NESTED reason flags (any subset, possibly none) and, for an explicit abort, bits 24-31 hold the code given to ck_pr_rtm_abort (CK_PR_RTM_CODE(x) = (x >> 24) & 0xff, line 62). The asm has a memory clobber (a compiler barrier).
note: gcc/x86_64/ck_pr_rtm.h:55-76 read in full. All four reviewers' points mean the old contract was weaker or wrong: the success-iff-~0U statement is the only thing the C code itself guarantees (r starts at ~0U); the claim that at least one low reason bit is set is from the hardware definition and not guaranteed by this file, so it was weakened to 'any subset, possibly none'. Contract left empty because the result depends on hardware abort behaviour.

Precondition: key points to len readable bytes and is read through a const uint32_t * (4-byte aligned on strict-alignment targets; the code does not check this); len is the byte length. Postcondition: it sets h1 = (uint32_t)seed ^ len and h2 = (uint32_t)(seed >> 32); while len >= 8 it consumes two 32-bit words, mixing each with the constant multiplier 0x5bd1e995 into h1 and h2; if 4 or more bytes remain it consumes one more word into h1; the remaining 1-3 bytes (switch on len, with fall-through) are XORed into h2 which is then multiplied by m; it then applies the final avalanche steps to h1 and h2 and returns the 64-bit value (h1 << 32) | h2 (234-284). It only reads the input and has no error return; a negative len skips the loops and the tail switch, and is XORed into h1 at line 239.

Postcondition: it first scans the list for a node whose Path is equal (case-sensitive strcmp, 1010) to ExternalPath. If found: when that node has ACPI_EXT_ORIGIN_FROM_OPCODE it returns AE_ALREADY_EXISTS at once with no change (1016-1018); otherwise (else-branch) it raises Type from ACPI_TYPE_ANY to the given Type when the new Type is not ANY (1023-1026), then in either of the non-opcode cases lowers Value to the new Value if smaller (1031-1034), ORs Flags into the node's Flags and clears ACPI_EXT_INTERNAL_PATH_ALLOCATED (1038-1039), and returns AE_ALREADY_EXISTS; no node is created and the caller still owns both path strings. If not found it allocates a zeroed node with ACPI_ALLOCATE_ZEROED and returns AE_NO_MEMORY if that fails, with the list unchanged (1049-1053); otherwise it records Flags, Value, Path, Type, Length = strlen(ExternalPath) and InternalPath, and inserts the node before the first existing entry for which AcpiUtStricmp(new path, entry path) < 0 (a case-insensitive ordering, 1071), else at the tail, becoming the head when the list is empty, and returns AE_OK, after which the list owns the node and the strings (1068-1099).
note: dmextern.c:987-1100, slice cut head and name wrong. Round-17 reviewer WRONG: duplicate detection is case-sensitive strcmp (1010); only the ordering uses case-insensitive AcpiUtStricmp (1071). Old prose otherwise accurate; the Type upgrade only applies when the existing node is not from an opcode (1023 is an else-if of the 1016 test).

name: AcpiDmUnresolvedWarning
prose: Slice cut the head: void AcpiDmUnresolvedWarning(UINT8 Type) is at dmextern.c:1748-1843 (the packet name is not in the file). Precondition: Type selects the output form (nonzero = comment block through AcpiOsPrintf, zero = fprintf to stderr); the globals AcpiGbl_NumExternalMethods, AcpiGbl_ResolvedExternalMethods and AcpiGbl_ExternalFileList are valid. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns at once, printing nothing, when AcpiGbl_NumExternalMethods is 0 or equals AcpiGbl_ResolvedExternalMethods (1757-1765). Otherwise it picks Format as a ' *' pad string for nonzero Type and an empty string for zero, and itself fills the static buffers ExternalWarningPart1 (counts of external methods, resolved and unresolved), Part2 (examples of the -e option), Part3 (the -fe option) and Part4 with sprintf (1769-1806); the old assumption that Part1 is filled by the caller is wrong. For nonzero Type it calls AcpiOsPrintf with a ' /* ... */' block holding Parts 1, 2, 3 and 4 when AcpiGbl_ExternalFileList is NULL, or Parts 1, 3 and 4 when it is non-NULL (1810-1824). For zero Type it fprintf's to stderr Parts 1, 2 and 3 when AcpiGbl_ExternalFileList is NULL, or Parts 1 and 3 otherwise, without Part 4 (1828-1841). It writes the static buffers (which is a hazard if called concurrently) and acquires no locks or references.
note: dmextern.c:1743-1843 read in full. Old prose omitted both early returns (1757-1765) and wrongly assumed ExternalWarningPart1 was already filled; the printing combinations were right. Slice cut head, name was the only reviewer reason.

name: AdParseTable
prose: Slice cut the head: ACPI_STATUS AdParseTable(ACPI_TABLE_HEADER *Table, ACPI_OWNER_ID *OwnerId, BOOLEAN LoadTable, BOOLEAN External) is at dmtables.c:490-619. Precondition: Table is NULL or points to a readable table with a valid header and Length; OwnerId is NULL or writable; the global root table list and parse state are initialised. Postcondition: returns AE_NOT_EXIST if Table is NULL (504-506). Otherwise it prints 'Pass 1 parse', computes the AML start and length from Table->Length, sets the integer width from the table revision, creates the root scope op into the global AcpiGbl_ParseOpRoot with AcpiPsCreateScopeOp and returns AE_NO_MEMORY if that is NULL (520-523), creates a walk state and returns AE_NO_MEMORY if that fails (539-542), and returns the failing status of AcpiDsInitAmlWalk (545-549) or AcpiPsParseAml (554-557) if either fails (so these returns happen before the table is stored and before any owner id is allocated). It sets TableIndex to the last entry of the root table list (562). If LoadTable is true it calls AdStoreTable, then AcpiTbAllocateOwnerId, then, only if OwnerId is non-NULL, AcpiTbGetOwnerId writing the id to *OwnerId, returning the first failing status of these (566-585); so on an error return partway the table may be stored without an owner id. It then runs pass 2 with AcpiNsOneCompleteParse(ACPI_IMODE_LOAD_PASS2, TableIndex, NULL) and returns its status if it fails (590-593); if External is true it returns AE_OK (598-600); otherwise it parses deferred opcodes with AcpiDmParseDeferredOps (status ignored), finds resources with AcpiDmFindResources, prints 'Parsing completed' and returns AE_OK (607-618). The walk state is not freed by this function and AcpiGbl_ParseOpRoot is left set on all returns after its creation.
note: dmtables.c:490-619 read in full (comment lines skipped). Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: the LoadTable storage and owner id happen only after pass 1 succeeds (554-568) and the owner-id part can fail after the table is stored (573-583). Slice cut head; name outside slice was the other reason.

name: AcpiDmDumpHmat
prose: Slice cut the head: void AcpiDmDumpHmat(ACPI_TABLE_HEADER *Table) is at dmtbdump1.c:2395-2595. Precondition: Table points to a readable HMAT of at least Table->Length bytes; it is only read. Postcondition: returns nothing. It dumps the main HMAT header with AcpiDmDumpTable and returns if that fails (2411-2414). It then loops with Offset from sizeof(ACPI_TABLE_HMAT) while Offset < Table->Length: for each structure it prints a blank line, returns after printing 'Invalid HMAT structure length' if the structure's Length is below sizeof(ACPI_HMAT_STRUCTURE) (2425-2428), dumps the common structure header (return on failure), and switches on Type: ADDRESS_RANGE, LOCALITY and CACHE select a table info and a minimum body size; any other type prints '**** Unknown HMAT structure type 0x..' and jumps to NextSubtable, skipping the body (2457-2464, so unknown types are reported, not silently skipped). For the known types it returns after printing an error if HmatStruct->Length is below the body size, dumps the body (return on failure), and a second switch handles trailing data: LOCALITY loops over the initiator proximity domains (4 bytes each), the target proximity domains (4 bytes each) and the latency/bandwidth entries (2 bytes each, initiators times targets), and CACHE loops over the SMBIOS handles (2 bytes each); before each loop it checks that the remaining bytes of the structure suffice and returns after printing an 'Invalid ... number' message otherwise; a failing AcpiDmDumpTable in any loop returns; the ADDRESS_RANGE type and the second switch's default do nothing more (2483-2588). At NextSubtable it advances Offset by HmatStruct->Length (2593). It allocates nothing, takes no locks and does not modify Table.
note: dmtbdump1.c:2395-2595 read in full. Round-15 and round-17 reviewers WRONG: the unknown-type message is printed by the first switch's default (2457-2460) before goto NextSubtable; only the second switch's default (2585-2587) is silent, and it is reached only for known types (ADDRESS_RANGE falls there). Slice cut head.

name: FlOpenMiscOutputFiles
prose: Slice cut the head: ACPI_STATUS FlOpenMiscOutputFiles(char *FilenamePrefix) is at aslfiles.c:924-1257 (the packet name OpenOutputFiles is not in the file). Precondition: FilenamePrefix is a valid prefix string and the AslGbl_* option flags, AslGbl_FileType and AcpiGbl_DebugAslConversion are initialised; the function writes the global AslGbl_Files[] table and, for the converter debug file, AcpiGbl_ConvDebugFile. Postcondition: it returns AE_OK at once, opening nothing, when AslGbl_FileType is ASL_INPUT_TYPE_BINARY_ACPI_TABLE (952-954). Otherwise it handles each enabled output in this order: hex dump, debug, cross-reference, listing, preprocessor, user preprocessor; for each, FlGenerateFilename is called and a NULL result makes the function report an error with AslCommonError and return AE_ERROR (the message id is ASL_MSG_LISTING_FILENAME for the hex dump and listing files, ASL_MSG_DEBUG_FILENAME for the debug and cross-reference files, ASL_MSG_PREPROCESSOR_FILENAME for the two preprocessor files), leaving earlier files open; otherwise the file is opened with FlOpenFile (which the comment in the packet says terminates on open failure; that function was not read) and, for the hex, debug, cross-reference and listing files, written with the compiler signon and file header (the preprocessor files get neither). The debug file is opened by freopen onto stderr; if that returns NULL the function prints a message to stdout, calls CmCleanupAndExit and exit(1) instead of returning (992-1007). If AslGbl_FileType is ASL_INPUT_TYPE_ASCII_DATA it then returns AE_OK (1085-1087). Otherwise it opens the source output file unconditionally (FILE_SUFFIX_SOURCE, binary mode; AE_ERROR with ASL_MSG_LISTING_FILENAME if the name is NULL, 1092-1105), and then, each only when its flag is set, the assembly source, C source, C offset table, assembly include, C include, namespace and converter debug files, each with the same NULL-name AE_ERROR rule (ASL_MSG_LISTING_FILENAME) and with signon/header output (the C files also get an opening '/*' line); for the converter debug file it also sets AcpiGbl_ConvDebugFile to the new handle (1253). It returns AE_OK at the end (1256).
note: aslfiles.c:924-1257 read (signon/header lines skimmed; FlOpenFile not read). Old prose omitted the early AE_OK for binary ACPI tables (952-954), the exit(1) path for the debug file (1002-1006) and said ASL_MSG_LISTING_FILENAME 'for all remaining files' which is wrong for the debug and cross-reference messages (984, 1020) and misattributed the hex dump. Slice cut head; the unconditional source output was missing.

name: LdNamespace1Begin
prose: Slice cut the head: ACPI_STATUS LdNamespace1Begin(ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT *Op, UINT32 Level, void *Context) is at aslload.c:507-1018 (the packet name AcpiDmLoadDescendingOp is not in the file). It is the descending-op callback for load pass 1; Context is the ACPI_WALK_STATE. Precondition: Op is a valid ASL parse object, WalkState has a valid scope stack. Postcondition: for AML_INDEX_FIELD_OP, AML_BANK_FIELD_OP and AML_FIELD_OP it returns the status of LdLoadFieldElements (541-548); an AML_INT_CONNECTION_OP whose first child is a NAMEPATH does an AcpiNsLookup and then continues with the common code; it returns AE_OK immediately if Op->Asl.Node is already set (577-579). For a NAMESEG, NAMESTRING or METHODCALL op whose parent is a named object (and that is not a method call) it returns AE_OK; otherwise it looks the name up with AcpiNsLookup (no scope opening), and AE_NOT_FOUND sets OP_NOT_FOUND_DURING_LOAD unless the parent is a package and returns AE_OK, other failures return their status, and success also returns from this branch (583-643). If Op->Asl.Namepath is NULL it returns AE_OK (646-649). Otherwise it derives ObjectType and flags from Op->Asl.ParseOpcode (NAME: from the bitwise type of the value; EXTERNAL: the declared type with ACPI_NS_EXTERNAL; DEFAULT_ARG: LdLoadResourceElements for resource descriptors; SCOPE: its own lookup path; default: AslMapNamedOpcodeToDataType). The SCOPE case looks the path up, on AE_NOT_FOUND tries to create a scope with ACPI_TYPE_LOCAL_SCOPE and returns that failure if it fails, or reports not-found/namepath-does-not-exist errors and goes to FinishNode, and for an existing node may change its type to LOCAL_SCOPE (reporting a remark/error) and pushes the scope with AcpiDsScopeStackPush, returning that status on failure (723-862). For the common path it sets ACPI_NS_ERROR_IF_FOUND (and ACPI_NS_PREFIX_MUST_EXIST for named/create opcodes except EXTERNAL) and calls AcpiNsLookup in load-pass-1 mode: AE_ALREADY_EXISTS is handled by retyping a LOCAL_SCOPE node, calling LdAnalyzeExternals for external declarations (an AE_ERROR from it is turned into AE_OK and, on failure, returned; success continues, 910-939), or reporting a duplicate-name error and returning AE_OK (942-956); AE_NOT_FOUND (a missing prefix) falls back to the root node with AE_OK (959-967); any other failure is reported and returned (969-975). It then calls LdCheckSpecialNames, pushes a new scope when ForceNewScope is set (returning its failure status), and sets Node->Op = Op (994) except in the paths that jump past it; at FinishNode it sets Op->Asl.Node = Node, and for PARSEOP_METHOD sets Node->Value to the argument count (Op->Asl.Extra), and for an EXTERNAL method that is still external sets Node->Value to the declared argument count (1000-1015), and returns Status. It may emit compiler errors and remarks through AslError. Partly read: the lines were read with comment and message-printing lines filtered, and the Node->Op assignment condition around 989-994 was not re-read.
note: aslload.c:507-1018. PARTLY READ: read in two filtered passes (507-770, 767-1040); the exact conditions of the Node->Op assignment (about 989-994) and the first half of the SCOPE not-found branch (about 734-760) are summarised, not verified line by line. Slice cut head; name outside slice was the only reviewer reason.

name: MtMethodAnalysisWalkEnd
prose: Slice cut the head: ACPI_STATUS MtMethodAnalysisWalkEnd(ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT *Op, UINT32 Level, void *Context) is at aslmethod.c:914-1104 (the ascending-pass callback of the method analysis walk; Context is an ASL_ANALYSIS_WALK_INFO whose MethodStack top is MethodInfo). Precondition: Op is a visited parse node and, for PARSEOP_METHOD and PARSEOP_RETURN, MethodInfo is non-NULL. Postcondition: for PARSEOP_METHOD or PARSEOP_RETURN with a NULL MethodInfo it prints 'No method info for method!', reports ASL_MSG_COMPILER_INTERNAL, calls CmCleanupAndExit and returns AE_AML_INTERNAL (929-937, return reached only if CmCleanupAndExit returns); in every other case it returns AE_OK at 1103. It then switches on Op->Asl.ParseOpcode: PARSEOP_METHOD pops the method from WalkInfo->MethodStack, counts an implicit no-value return when the last statement is not a Return and OP_HAS_NO_EXIT is not set, warns ASL_MSG_RETURN_TYPES when the method has both value-returning and no-value returns, sets OP_METHOD_SOME_NO_RETVAL or OP_METHOD_NO_RETVAL on the method op when there are no-value returns, runs the predefined-name and GPE/_REG checks (ApCheckForPredefinedMethod, ApCheckForGpeNameConflict, ApCheckRegMethod) and frees MethodInfo with ACPI_FREE (947-1023); PARSEOP_NAME calls ApCheckForGpeNameConflict (1025-1030); PARSEOP_RETURN calls ApCheckPredefinedReturnValue, sets OP_HAS_NO_EXIT on its parent, sets Op->Asl.ParentMethod to the method's op and, if Op->Asl.Next exists, reports ASL_WARNING ASL_MSG_UNREACHABLE_CODE on that next node (1032-1060); PARSEOP_IF marks a directly following ELSE node with OP_IF_HAS_NO_EXIT when the IF has OP_HAS_NO_EXIT (1062-1075); PARSEOP_ELSE sets OP_HAS_NO_EXIT on its parent when both the ELSE and its IF-flag are set (1077-1088); any other opcode copies OP_HAS_NO_EXIT to the parent when the node has it and has a parent (1091-1099).
note: aslmethod.c:914-1104 read except comment lines and a few message-only lines. Old prose said 'always returns AE_OK' and omitted the METHOD and NAME cases and the internal-error return; those are wrong/missing (929-937, 947-1030). Slice cut head; name was the other reason.

name: TrLinkOpChildren
prose: Slice cut the head and the packet name TrLinkChildren is not in the file: the function is ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT *TrLinkOpChildren(ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT *Op, UINT32 NumChildren, ...) at asltree.c:457-632. Precondition: Op is a valid parse object and NumChildren is the number of ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT * arguments actually passed after it (any may be NULL). Postcondition: it calls va_start and TrSetOpEndLineNumber(Op) (which sets EndLine/EndLogicalLine from the current line numbers only if EndLine is still zero). For Op->Asl.ParseOpcode == PARSEOP_ASL_CODE it redirects the work: the first time (AslGbl_ParseTreeRoot NULL) it makes Op the tree root and changes its opcode to PARSEOP_DEFAULT_ARG, and for subsequent definition blocks it replaces Op with AslGbl_ParseTreeRoot (481-497); the other opcodes in that switch only print debug text. So the Op returned and the one that receives the children can be the existing root rather than the Op that was passed in. When AcpiGbl_CaptureComments is set and a pending AslGbl_CommentListHead exists, it stores it in Op->Asl.EndBlkComment and clears the list head and tail (524-539). For each argument it takes the child; if the child is non-NULL and identical to the previous child it reports ASL_WARNING ASL_MSG_COMPILER_INTERNAL ('Child op list invalid'), calls va_end and returns Op immediately (549-555), leaving earlier children linked; a NULL child is replaced by a new PARSEOP_DEFAULT_ARG op from TrAllocateOp (565-568); the first child becomes Op->Asl.Child, except that if Op already has a PARSEOP_DEFINITION_BLOCK child it is appended after that child's last sibling (572-595); every later child is linked as the previous child's Next (604-607); each child, and each peer chained after it, gets Parent = Op (600, 613-617). At the end it calls va_end, sets AslGbl_CommentState.LatestParseOp = Op when AcpiGbl_CaptureComments is set (625-627) and returns Op (631), which is the possibly redirected Op. It allocates memory only for DEFAULT_ARG placeholders and takes no locks.
note: asltree.c:457-632 read in full except debug prints. The old prose said it 'always returns Op' and omitted the ASL_CODE redirection (481-497) and the end-line side effect (474); the other described behaviours (comment list, NULL placeholder, duplicate-child early return, DEFINITION_BLOCK append) match the code. Slice cut the head; name outside slice was the only reviewer reason.

name: XfNamespaceLocateBegin
prose: Slice is the middle of ACPI_STATUS XfNamespaceLocateBegin(ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT *Op, UINT32 Level, void *Context) at aslxref.c:409-1008 (the packet gives no name); it is the descending-op callback of the cross-reference namespace walk and Context is the ACPI_WALK_STATE. Precondition: Op is a visited parse node with a known AML opcode, WalkState->ScopeInfo is the scope used for lookups. Postcondition: it first, for a method op with a node, allocates the node's MethodLocals and MethodArgs arrays if absent and records the argument count and per-argument flags (442-491). It then returns AE_OK without lookup for name declarations (501-503), handles local-variable and method-argument opcodes by marking the referenced or initialised LocalX/ArgX in the parent method's arrays (returning AE_OK, including when there is no parent method, 510-578), returns AE_OK for opcodes that carry no name (585-592), and for NAMESTRING/NAMESEG and named or create opcodes computes the path and object type and increments AslGbl_NsLookupCount before calling AcpiNsLookup (657-659). If AcpiNsLookup fails: an AE_NOT_FOUND on a CondRefOf operand is ignored silently, otherwise the failure is reported through AslError with a message that depends on the kind of name; after reporting, Status is set to AE_OK and returned, so a lookup failure is reported but the function returns AE_OK (659-762). If the lookup succeeds it checks the reference with XfValidateCrossReference and reports a temporary-object error (returning Status, 767-771), checks for an illegal forward reference when OP_NOT_FOUND_DURING_LOAD is set (776-815), may optimise the name path (OptOptimizeNamePath), validates field and resource tag lengths with warnings, calls OpcGenerateAmlOpcode in the relevant parent cases (981) and finally returns AE_OK (1007). The function can emit many compiler errors and warnings and allocates the per-method arrays that it stores in the namespace nodes.
note: aslxref.c:409-1008. PARTLY READ: I read the head (409-520), the lookup-failure region (655-775) and filtered return/branch lines for 775-1008; the tag/field length validation (871-955) and the optimisation conditions (817-860) are summarised, not verified line by line. Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: after an AslError the status is set to AE_OK (759) and returned (762), so lookup failures are returned as AE_OK.

name: CvPlaceComment
prose: Slice cut the head: void CvPlaceComment(UINT8 Type, char *CommentString) is at cvcompiler.c:970-1029. Precondition: CommentString is a NUL-terminated string that outlives its use (it is stored by pointer in several cases); AslGbl_CommentState.LatestParseOp must be non-NULL for ASLCOMMENT_INLINE, ASL_COMMENT_CLOSE_BRACE and, when ParsingParenBraceNode is NULL, ASL_COMMENT_CLOSE_PAREN (those cases dereference it, 992, 1014, 1022; there is no NULL check). Postcondition: returns nothing; it reads LatestParseNode and ParenBraceNode from AslGbl_CommentState and switches on Type: ASL_COMMENT_STANDARD calls CvAddToCommentList(CommentString), which appends a new comment node (CvCommentNodeCalloc) at the tail of the global comment list with Comment = CommentString (the string pointer itself, 893-910); ASLCOMMENT_INLINE sets the latest parse node's InlineComment to CvAppendInlineComment(old, CommentString); ASL_COMMENT_OPEN_PAREN does the same on the global AslGbl_InlineCommentBuffer; ASL_COMMENT_CLOSE_PAREN does the same on ParenBraceNode->Asl.EndNodeComment when ParenBraceNode is non-NULL, else on LatestParseNode->Asl.EndNodeComment; ASL_COMMENT_CLOSE_BRACE sets LatestParseNode->Asl.CloseBraceComment = CommentString (stores the pointer, no copy); any other Type does nothing (997-1028). CvAppendInlineComment(InlineComment, ToAdd) returns ToAdd itself (not a copy) when InlineComment is NULL and InlineComment itself when ToAdd is NULL, otherwise it allocates a new string of the two concatenated from UtLocalCacheCalloc (935-952), so the caller's string pointer can be stored directly in the inline, open-paren and close-paren cases as well as the standard and close-brace cases. Nothing is returned.
note: cvcompiler.c:893-953, 970-1029 read in full. Both reviewers RIGHT: lifetime/NULL preconditions for INLINE and CLOSE_PAREN (992, 1014) and the pointer returned by CvAppendInlineComment when the old comment is NULL (936-938). Side finding: CvAppendInlineComment writes Str[Size + 1] = 0 (951) into a Size + 1 byte allocation, one byte past the end; not part of this function's claim.

name: DtLookupLabel
prose: Precondition: Name points to a NUL-terminated string (it is dereferenced at once, so it must not be NULL), AslGbl_LabelList is NULL or the head of a NextLabel-linked list whose entries have a valid Value string. Postcondition (dtexpress.c:507-535): if the first character of Name is '$' it advances Name by one (one leading '$' only). It then walks the list from AslGbl_LabelList in order and returns the first DT_FIELD whose Value equals Name by strcmp, or NULL when the list is empty or no entry matches. It reads the list only; it allocates nothing, frees nothing and takes no locks.
note: dtexpress.c:507-535 read in full; the function name (DtLookupLabel) is in the file, the packet name was truncated, hence the earlier 'dropped' rounds. Old prose correct.

name: DtCompileIort
prose: Slice cut the head: ACPI_STATUS DtCompileIort(void **List) is at dttable1.c:2634-3033. Precondition: List points to the DT_FIELD list for an IORT; the subtable stack has the parent table pushed (DtPeekSubtable). Postcondition: it compiles the main IORT header with DtCompileTable and returns its failure status (2661-2665); it returns AE_ERROR after DtError(ASL_MSG_UNSUPPORTED) if the table revision is 1, 2 or 4 (2674-2677); it compiles the optional padding (DtCompileTable into the pad info, returning a failure status, 2694-2698; if no padding subtable results it compiles generic data, 2707-2711). It then loops over the remaining fields, compiling a node header (AcpiDmTableInfoIortHdr for revision 0, IortHdr3 for revision 3 and above, failure status returned) and switches on the node type: ITS_GROUP, NAMED_COMPONENT, PCI_ROOT_COMPLEX, SMMU, SMMU_V3, PMCG and RMR each compile their own table info and trailing lists, returning any DtCompileTable failure status; an unrecognized node type calls DtFatal(ASL_MSG_UNKNOWN_SUBTABLE) and returns AE_ERROR (2989-2990). For NAMED_COMPONENT the padding step compiles IortNode padding fields; only when that DtCompileTable produces no subtable (Subtable is NULL, the else-branch) does it compare NodeLength with IortNode->MappingOffset: it returns AE_BAD_DATA if NodeLength is greater, and if NodeLength is smaller it compiles DtCompilePadding of the difference (returning a failure status) and sets NodeLength = MappingOffset (2797-2829); when a padding subtable was compiled, NodeLength simply grows by its length (2804-2808). After the type-specific part each node's MappingOffset is set from NodeLength, the ID mappings are compiled and counted in MappingCount, and MappingOffset is forced to 0 when the mapping count is 0 (2995-3019); the node count is stored in Iort->NodeCount and AE_OK is returned (3031-3032). Compiled subtables are inserted into the parent table as they are produced, so on every error return the subtables compiled so far remain inserted.
note: dttable1.c:2634-3033. PARTLY READ: head, status/return lines and the NAMED_COMPONENT region (2797-2830) were read line by line; the per-node-type bodies (2745-2990) were read through their DtCompileTable/return lines only, so the exact SMMU/RMR offset and count assignments are not re-verified here. Round-15 reviewer RIGHT: AE_BAD_DATA is only returned in the Subtable == NULL branch (2809-2813), not whenever NodeLength exceeds MappingOffset.

name: DtCompilePhat
prose: Slice cut the head: ACPI_STATUS DtCompilePhat(void **List) is at dttable2.c:1250-1490. Precondition: List points to the DT_FIELD list pointer positioned at PHAT subtable records (the function itself does not compile a main PHAT header, only the records; I did not check where the main header is compiled); for FW_HEALTH_DATA the list must contain at least four more fields (three Next links are followed to the offset field and a fourth to the device-path field without NULL checks, 1306-1327), the offset field's Value being a hexadecimal string and the device-path field's Value a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: loop while *PFieldList is non-NULL: compile the record header with DtCompileTable (failure status returned), insert it into DtPeekSubtable() and push it with DtPushSubtable (1275-1286); switch on the header type: FW_VERSION_DATA selects info Phat0 and sets the header Length to sizeof(ACPI_PHAT_VERSION_DATA); FW_HEALTH_DATA parses the offset field with sscanf, computes the device-path length (twice the string length plus a terminator, 1331), sets TableOffset, and, only if the parsed offset is nonzero, overwrites the offset field's Value text with TableOffset via snprintf (1340-1343), selects Phat1 and sets Length to sizeof(ACPI_PHAT_HEALTH_DATA); any other type calls DtFatal(ASL_MSG_UNKNOWN_SUBTABLE) and returns AE_ERROR (1358-1361). It then compiles the selected body (failure status returned) and inserts it. For FW_VERSION_DATA it compiles ElementCount version elements (Phat0a), inserting each and adding sizeof(ACPI_PHAT_VERSION_ELEMENT) to the header Length, then DtPopSubtable (1380-1406). For FW_HEALTH_DATA it compiles the device-path part (Phat1a, failure status returned) and inserts it; if the field list is then empty it returns AE_OK at once without popping the subtable pushed at 1286 (1430-1434); otherwise it adds the length, re-reads the offset value, compiles the device-specific data (Phat1b) only when the offset is nonzero (failure status returned), adds its length to the header, and pops the subtable (1441-1476). A second switch default for an unknown type also returns AE_ERROR (1482-1485). When the list ends it returns Status (AE_OK, 1489). On every error return the subtables built so far stay inserted and pushed ones are not popped.
note: dttable2.c:1250-1490 read in full (debug print lines skipped). Round-15 reviewer: its claim that the main PHAT table is compiled by this function is not borne out: the function body starts straight at the record loop (1271) and compiles only records; whether a caller compiles the main header was not checked. The old prose's claims (early AE_OK without pop at 1433, DtFatal AE_ERROR returns at 1360 and 1484) are correct.

name: DtCompileMadt
prose: Slice cut the head: ACPI_STATUS DtCompileMadt(void **List) is at dttable2.c:249-469. Precondition: List points to the DT_FIELD list of a MADT; the subtable stack has the parent table on top once the main MADT table is compiled (it is compiled and inserted by this function). Postcondition: it compiles the main MADT table with DtCompileTable (AcpiDmTableInfoMadt) and returns that status on failure with the stack unchanged (263-267); inserts it into DtPeekSubtable() and reads Revision from the parent buffer (270-274). It then loops while fields remain: DtCompileTable of a MADT subtable header (failure status returned before anything is pushed, 279-283), insert it under the parent and DtPushSubtable it (287-288), then select a body info table from MadtHeader->Type: types 0-27 map to AcpiDmTableInfoMadt0..Madt27, with revision-dependent variants for GENERIC_INTERRUPT (Revision > 6: Madt11b, == 6: Madt11a, else Madt11), GENERIC_REDISTRIBUTOR (Revision > 6: Madt14a, else Madt14) and GENERIC_TRANSLATOR (Revision > 6: Madt15a, else Madt15); a type >= ACPI_MADT_TYPE_OEM_RESERVED uses AcpiDmTableInfoMadt128; any other type calls DtFatal(ASL_MSG_UNKNOWN_SUBTABLE) and returns AE_ERROR with the header still pushed (292-452). It compiles the body (a failure status is returned with the header still pushed, 457-461), inserts it under DtPeekSubtable() and calls DtPopSubtable (463-465). It returns AE_OK when the field list is empty (468). So the stack is balanced on AE_OK and on a failure of the first two DtCompileTable calls, but not when the unknown-type error or a body compile failure returns.

name: AcpiDbCommandDispatch
prose: Slice cut the head: ACPI_STATUS AcpiDbCommandDispatch(char *InputBuffer, ACPI_WALK_STATE *WalkState, ACPI_PARSE_OBJECT *Op) is at dbinput.c:895-1397. Precondition: InputBuffer is a NUL-terminated command line; WalkState and Op may be NULL (Op is non-NULL when dispatched from inside a method). Postcondition: Status starts as AE_CTRL_TRUE (906). It returns AE_CTRL_TERMINATE at once if AcpiGbl_DbTerminateLoop is already set (911-913). Otherwise it parses the line with AcpiDbGetLine into AcpiGbl_DbArgs, matches the command, and adds the line to the history (926-928, not for the history-last command), and if fewer than the command's MinArgs parameters were given it prints the usage and returns AE_CTRL_TRUE (933-941). It then switches on the command and runs its handler; handlers that return a status (for example find, methods, objects, stats, sleep, fields via AcpiDbDisplayFields and others) store it in Status. The returns that leave the switch early are: AE_OK for the null command with Op set (950-952), for 'fields' with an invalid address space id (1034), for 'go' (1043) and for the step-into case when Op is set (1098); AE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED for 'stop' (1221); the status of a failed AcpiEnable (1259); AE_CTRL_TRUE for a history command whose lookup fails (1066, 1077) and, for a history command that succeeds, the status of the recursive AcpiDbCommandDispatch on the retrieved line (1069-1070, 1080-1081); AE_CTRL_TERMINATE for the exit/quit command (after setting AcpiGbl_DbTerminateLoop, 1382-1383) and for a method-terminate case (1370-1371); and AE_CTRL_TRUE for an unknown command (1388-1389). When the switch is left by break, the function returns Status, except that any successful status, including the AE_OK that 'call' sets (989), is converted to AE_CTRL_TRUE (1392-1397); a failing status from a handler is returned unchanged. So AE_CTRL_TRUE is the normal return after a successfully executed command. The function writes the global argument arrays and the history buffer and may print through AcpiOsPrintf; it acquires no locks.
